title: The Law and the Humanity of Christ
english: When speaking of mysteries. Especially since his parents were eager to circumcise him when he was an eight-day-old child, just as the evangelist Luke reports. And they subsequently brought him into the temple to present him to the Lord, performing the pure offerings, to give a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.

Therefore, if he was being presented with the pure gifts according to the law, and bore the circumcision at eight days, it is written that he was not unsuitably made under the law. Nor was the Word subject to the law, as the informers glory, being the law himself; nor did God need pure sacrifices, cleansing all things instantly by a single thought and sanctifying. But even if, having taken the human organ from the virgin, he bore it and became under the law, having been purified according to the value of the firstborn, he did not remain requesting the provision of these things, but so that he might ransom those who were sold by the judgment of the curse.

For the man who died, having risen after three days, cries out to Mary, who was eager to touch the holy members, having received back: 'Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God' (Acts 10:41). And the saying, 'I have not yet ascended to my Father,' was not spoken by the Word, being God and rushing from heaven and being sustained in the bosom of the Father, nor by Wisdom, who contains all created things; but he, the one being harmonized from all directions as a man, permitted this, he who was raised from the dead, having not yet ascended to the Father after death, but being stored up as the firstfruits of the procession.

And he clearly names the crucified man as Lord of Glory, writing: since he also made him both Lord and Christ, as the apostles say they were in agreement with sensible Israel: 'Let every house of Israel know securely, then, that God made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ' (Acts 2:32, 2:36). He made the Jesus who was suffering Lord, and not the Wisdom, nor the Word, who holds the power of lordship from above, but the one whose hands were stretched out toward the heavens by the cross. If he is incorporeal, he neither falls under the touch of hands, nor [to] sensible eyes...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG 18 Oratio in illud Dominus creavit me u01-rem-early

title: The Divine Power and the Humanity of Christ
english: He is contained: he does not suffer by enduring, he is not approached by calamities, he does not share in death, he is not hidden in the earth, he is not shut in a tomb, and he does not rise from monuments. No one takes the soul from me; I have authority to lay down my soul, and I have authority to take it again. And if he had the authority of both like God, he allowed them to act foolishly in the young man they were handling, but he worked more excellently in those rising. It has been shown by an irrefutable vote that he himself, working through himself, raised his own house. And the great works of the Son should also be attributed to the most divine Father. For neither does a Son create without the Father, according to the decisions of the torn sacred writings. For this very reason, it is written that the most divine Begetter raised Christ from the dead; and again, the Son promises to raise his own temple.

If, therefore, the divine Spirit of Christ has been shown to be indifferent to the things examined before, then those who enter into the apostolic boundaries are excessively concerned. For if Paul spoke of the Lord of glory being crucified, clearly looking toward the man, this will not cause him to apply passion to the Divine. What, then, are they weaving together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?

If it were indeed fitting to surround him with the appearance of weakness, someone might say it was consistent for the man to attach these things to himself, but certainly not to the fullness of deity, or to the dignity of the highest Wisdom, or to God described by Paul as being over all. This is indeed the way of weakness, through which it is written according to Paul that one reaches death; for man lives by the power of God, clearly sharing with the divine Spirit; since the one believing in him has also been shown to be the power of the Most High according to the terms that have passed away.

If, having mounted the virgin womb, he did not diminish his authority, nor does the Spirit suffer harm when the wood of the cross fastens the body. For the body was indeed crucified as a mere shell, but the divine Spirit of Wisdom passed through the body, and mounted the heavens, and encompassed all the earth, and held the abysses, and discerning each soul, distinguished them, and did all things simultaneously as God did. For the highest Wisdom, having been brought down, is not contained within the physical masses, just as the elements of the moist and dry are within the vessels...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Power and the Council of Nicaea
english: They are being seized, or rather encompassed, rather than they encompass the spheres. But a certain divine and unutterable power, encompassing the innermost and outermost of the nebula, strengthens them, and having sounded through from here and there, it holds all the masses together, encompassing them.

If the sun, being a visible body and perceptible by sense, endures such and such ravages everywhere on earth without changing its order, or feeling a small or large wound, we should think that the incorporeal Wisdom endures the same, and does not change her nature, even if her temple is fastened to a cross, or undergoes dissolution, or suffers wounding, or receives corruption. But the nebula suffers, while the unclouded essence has established its value as entirely pure.

I proceed from here already even to the things accomplished. What then? Since because of these things the assembly at Nicaea arrives greatest, perhaps even two hundred and seventy in number being gathered together (for the exact number I am not able to write because of the crowd of many men, since I do not investigate all this with great care), and as the way of the faith was being sought, the letter of Eusebius was being put forward as a clear proof, a blasphemy. And after all was read, it immediately increased the unmeasured disaster of the defection for those who had heard it, and provided unendurable shame to the writer. And since the work of those concerning Eusebius was clearly caught, some of a device, putting forward the name of peace, tearing apart the unlawful letter in the sight of all, silenced all those accustomed to speak best.

But the Arian ones, fearing lest they should be ostracized from such a same assembly, first anathematize the forbidden doctrine, having signed with their own hands agreeing letters. And having held the presidencies through most of the circuit, it is necessary for them to take a pretext, sometimes through oblivion, sometimes obviously, to represent the rejected opinions, attacking the proofs in various ways. Wishing to fix the weed-like fabrications, they condemn the overseers; and in this way they wage war against the preachers of piety. But we do not believe that atheistic men can ever hold fast to the divine. For even if they should be strong again, they shall be defeated again according to the solemn-sounding prophet Isaiah.
